title: Sources for the future-mode world map: climate projections by country and by state or province, and the region shapes they join to
need: The site is adding a 'future mode': a world map of projected climate for every country and, inside a country, for every state or province. A projection is a 20-year window under a named emissions path, shown with the range across the climate models beside the median. That needs two things. First, open projection values for countries and for states or provinces, for measures people can feel: days at 35 °C or more, hot nights, the hottest day, the wettest day, dry spells and warming. Second, region shapes whose codes join to those values by a declared rule, never by a guess. The values and the simplified shapes are written to public JSON, so a source whose terms forbid redistribution or derivatives cannot be used, and every number must keep its dataset version, file and licence.
method: Three scratch-note passes, kept outside the repo. (1) Projection sources: values read live from the CCKP API on 2026-10-15, nothing written. (2) Boundary files: read-only, file sizes from 'curl -sI' unless marked estimate. (3) An independent verification pass over (1) and (2): read-only (curl and in-memory range reads, nothing written), run on 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16.
Where the verification pass disagrees with the first two, this record follows the verification pass and lists each change under 'corrections'.
'decisions' come from the build plan for future mode, checked against the code on 2026-10-16.
The last two open questions (the wettest day, the Philippines) were decided later in the build. They are not in the scratch notes.

licence_terms_verbatim: A 'mandatory and binding addition': non-binding mediation, then after 45 days 'the UNCITRAL Arbitration Rules as then in force', with a sole arbitrator.

No Endorsement, and No Association: no name, trade-mark, emblem or logo without consent.
Third-party data 'may not be redistributed or reused without the consent of the original data provider, or may be subject to terms and conditions that are different from those described above.'
'These Dataset Terms incorporate the World Bank Terms and Conditions by reference.' (missed by both first passes; found by the verification pass)

candidates.proposed_licence_class: open (CC BY 4.0 with the additional terms above; already registered as wb-cckp)
candidates.granularity: 246 countries and 3,527 regions in 244 countries. Region detail is uneven: Latvia has 119 units, Malta 67 and Seychelles 60; India has 35, Kenya 47 (all counties) and Brazil 31. Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan have no regions. 68 units have placeholder names (an example is GBR.25639503, 'Administrative unit not available'). 32 DIS.* units are disputed areas with no names; they do have values.
candidates.variables: hd35 (maximum 35 °C or more), hd40 (40 °C or more), hi39 (heat index 39 °C or more), tr26 (nights 26 °C or more), txx (hottest day), wsdi (warm spell days), rx1day (wettest day), cdd (dry spell), spei12 (drought index) and tas (warming). Also available: hd30/42/45/50, hi35/37/41, tr (20 °C), tr23/29/32, rx5day, r20mm, r95ptot, fd, pr. The heatwave product ehf2 is covered in weighting_findings.
candidates.years: Windows 2020–2039, 2040–2059, 2060–2079 and 2080–2099, plus a 1995–2014 baseline (the models' own simulation of the past). Annual series 2015–2100.
candidates.scenarios: SSP1-1.9, 1-2.6, 2-4.5, 3-7.0 and 5-8.5. Percentiles p10, median and p90. Products: climatology and anomaly. Ensemble of 30 CMIP6 models.
candidates.weighting: Area-weighted. The metadata page describes 'fractional overlap' of grid cells plus 'cosine of latitude' weighting. There is no population-weighted variant of the threshold indicators (see weighting_findings).

values_read.what: Median of 30 CMIP6 models, 2040–2059, SSP2-4.5, read live on 2026-10-15. Days a year unless stated. The verification pass re-read the hd35 values (India, Nigeria, California, Delhi, Kenya, Brazil) and they matched; the other rows were read by the first pass only.
more: Delhi hd35 in 2080–2099 is 117.36 under SSP1-1.9 and 196.1 under SSP5-8.5.
hd35, 2040–2059, SSP2-4.5, median, read by the verification pass: Kenya 75.44, Brazil 47.25.
Kenya's regions are real: Turkana 162.43, Marsabit 133.9, Nairobi 0.

headline_checks.value: India 94.78, Kenya 75.44, Brazil 47.25 and Delhi (IND.11510) 123.28 days a year at 35 °C or more
headline_checks.query: GET the hd35 URL in file_urls with {geo} set to each code (verification pass, 2026-10-15/16). Nigeria 134.32, California 47.12 and the Delhi 1995–2014 baseline 102.09 also match.

headline_checks.value: 246 countries and 3,527 regions in 244 countries; India 35 regions, Kenya 47, Brazil 31
Asking for two variables at once works; all_subnationals returns data: []
headline_checks.query: GET with hd35,tas, and with all_subnationals (verification pass).

caveats: Area-weighted, not population-weighted. Say 'averaged over the land of the place'.
CCKP's national totals for count-type values (population and person-days) are 2–3 times the sum of its own regions. Never publish them (see weighting_findings).

The portal's Cartography tab says its numbers still use the previous World Bank boundaries. A July 2026 World Bank boundary release updated 'many ADM1 boundaries' and CCKP plans to switch. When it does, every region code changes.
CCKP does not document its region codes; its metadata page says only 'reflecting World Bank shapefiles for national (ADM0) and subnational (ADM1) units'.
The portal's web pages and geonames.json cannot be fetched by a script, so the names file may need a manual snapshot (rule 7).
India has no Jammu and Kashmir or Ladakh values at all (IND.11515 is missing).
candidates.verdict: Adopted as the source of the future values.
candidates.recommendation: Use for days at 35 °C or more, hot nights, the hottest day, the wettest day and dry spells by country and by region, labelled area-averaged (the wettest day was withheld later in the build: see open_questions). Never publish CCKP's national population or person-day totals.

candidates.naming_note: 'Legacy v1 (2020)' in the boundary note means the three 2020 admin-0-only files on the catalogue (geojson_highres 20,346,962 B, geojson_lowres 4,678,469 B, topojson 2,149,917 B). It is not this V1, which is dated 2025-05-07 and has admin-1.

candidates.licence_quote: License : Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 … This dataset is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (World Bank Official Boundaries catalogue, dataset 0038272, version 2026-09-10). The licence links to datacatalog.worldbank.org/public-licenses?fragment=cc, which says: 'CC-BY 4.0, with the additional terms below, is the default license for all Datasets produced by the World Bank itself and distributed as open data . All users of these Datasets under the CC-BY 4.0 License also agree to the following mandatory terms:' followed by the same mediation and UNCITRAL clause as in the Dataset Terms.
candidates.licence_inference: V1 itself carries no licence. The zip has no licence file or readme and its .shp.xml files have no use-constraint fields. The catalogue does not offer V1. The licence is therefore inferred from the catalogue's dataset-level CC BY 4.0 and from the zip's host, CCKP's open bucket. The bucket's AWS Open Data Registry entry is inconsistent: it reads License: '[World Bank Open Database License (ODbL)](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)', an ODbL label linking to CC BY 4.0. The worldbank/WB_GAD GitHub repo is MPL-2.0, but that covers documentation and code only.
candidates.proposed_licence_class: open, inferred (flagged for the owner: see open_questions)
candidates.granularity: ADM0, ADM1, ADM2 and the disputed areas the World Bank does not assign to a country (NDLSA). The admin-1 layer has 3,604 features. Admin-1 fields include GAUL_0, GAUL_1, HASC_1, ADM1CD_t and P_CODE_1_t (the GAUL rule below also uses WB_A3). The GAUL_0 field confirms that CCKP's number after the dot starts with the FAO GAUL country code.
candidates.years: Dated 2025-05-07; zip last modified 10 Jun 2025. Older than v2 (14 May 2026) and v3 (10 Sep 2026): for example the v2 maintenance log says Trindade/Martim Vaz, Rocas Atoll and Alcatrazes (BRA014–017) were folded into states in 2026, and CCKP's Brazil still has 4 'Name Unknown' island units.
candidates.sizes_and_formats: Shapefile zip, 264,700,182 B. The build plan notes that the admin-1 .shp may exceed the 200 MB max_bytes default and that the zip must be checked against the source's mirror_raw: true setting.

headline_checks.value: The GAUL rule {WB_A3}.{GAUL_0}{GAUL_1} matches 2,254 of CCKP's regions with names confirmed (USA, Brazil, France and China among them); the ADM1CD rule {WB_A3}.{GAUL_0}{int(ADM1CD_t[3:])} matches 467 with names confirmed. Together: 2,732 of 3,527 codes.
headline_checks.query: Verification pass: build the CCKP code from the V1 admin-1 fields and compare with all_countries_subnationals and the names file.

headline_checks.value: India matches 35 of 35 (IND010 Delhi becomes IND.11510 Delhi)
By name within the same country, 3,176 of 3,527 CCKP names appear in V1; 183 of 244 countries have equal counts with every name matched

caveats: No column holds the CCKP string as it is; the code has to be built by a rule.

Some countries need name or declared pairs: Kenya matches 47 of 47 by name but not by code (CCKP numbers Kenya's counties in a different order; Uasin Gishu = 1); Nigeria matches 35 of 37 by name (Akwa Ibom and Abuja unmatched).
Jammu and Kashmir sits in V1's disputed-areas layer.
68 CCKP units have placeholder names and 32 DIS.* units have none.

The only cartography duty on the World Bank's own boundaries applies to Bank staff ('staff must receive legal clearance … World Bank Cartography Unit'). The Dataset Terms still require attribution, pass-through of the acknowledgment, no endorsement and no logo.
The Philippines' Bangsamoro and Region 12 are on 2013 UN SALB shapes (see open_questions).
candidates.verdict: Adopted as the region map (admin-0 for the world map, admin-1 per country). The only downloadable boundary file whose codes join to CCKP's.
candidates.recommendation: Register it with the licence inference written down and the owner's decision recorded. Join to CCKP by the GAUL rule, then the ADM1CD rule, then declared pairs, then exact names (see decisions). Record every pair.

join_findings.summary: CCKP's region codes join to one downloadable boundary file: World Bank Official Boundaries (WB GAD) V1, dated 2025-05-07, in CCKP's own S3 bucket. They do not join to the current v3, to Natural Earth admin-1, to geoBoundaries or to GADM. The first boundary pass said they join to none of them; the verification pass found V1. V1 joins by a rule, not as it stands: no column holds the CCKP string, and the rules cover 2,732 of 3,527 codes, so names and declared pairs do the rest.

cckp_codes.format: ISO3.{GAUL country code}{n}. GAUL country codes seen: IND 115, KEN 133, BRA 37, USA 259, CHN 147295, EGY 40765, AFG 1. Examples: USA.2593214 (Alabama), IND.1151, IND.11510 (Delhi), CHN.147295898, FRA.851248 (Alsace), KSV.750081, DIS.990011.
cckp_codes.how_known: The first pass inferred the GAUL basis from the numbers and said the producer does not say so. The verification pass confirmed it with the GAUL_0 field in the V1 file.
cckp_codes.disputed_units: 32 DIS.* units, with no names. They have values.
cckp_codes.placeholder_names: 68 CCKP units have placeholder names. Brazil's 4 'Name Unknown' units are islands.
cckp_codes.names: The names file comes from the API itself (_format=xlsx gives a code, name column) or from geonames.json (a person has to download it).

join_findings.v1_layer: Admin-1 layer: 3,604 features. Fields include GAUL_0, GAUL_1, HASC_1, ADM1CD_t and P_CODE_1_t, and WB_A3 is used by the rules.

rules.name: GAUL rule
rules.names: Confirmed (USA, Brazil, France and China among them).

rules.name: ADM1CD rule
rules.example: India matches 35 of 35: IND010 Delhi becomes IND.11510 Delhi.

by_name.result: Within the same country, 3,176 of 3,527 CCKP names appear in V1. 183 of 244 countries have equal counts with every name matched (the first pass found 75 of 207 against v3).
by_name.kenya: 47 of 47 by name but not by code: CCKP numbers Kenya's counties in a different order (Uasin Gishu = 1).
by_name.nigeria: 35 of 37 by name; Akwa Ibom and Abuja unmatched.

files_that_do_not_join.file: World Bank Official Boundaries v3 (10 Sep 2026)
files_that_do_not_join.why: v3 uses different codes (ADM1CD_c, for example IND003 and FRA013) and the API returns nothing for them. The unit sets differ: the number of regions differs from CCKP's in 69 of 244 countries (FRA 23 against 13, LVA 119 against 43, UGA 111 against 4, VNM 63 against 34, MLT 67 against 6, SYC 60 against 7). By name, 2,210 of 3,500 named CCKP regions match exactly within the same country, and 75 of 207 countries match one-to-one. v2 (14 May 2026) merged Dadra and Nagar Haveli with Daman and Diu, and the v2 maintenance log records Brazil's island units folded into states in 2026. For India, the verification pass found that the current v3 matches 33 of the 35 codes 'by the same rule'; the other two do not map.

Natural Earth's admin-1 is not consistently the first level (GBR 232 counties, FRA 101 departments, SVN 193 municipalities, ITA 110 provinces, KEN 8 old provinces against 47 counties). CCKP's region names match in only 27 countries (40 ignoring accents and capitals). The 50m admin-1 file has 9 countries only and the 110m file has the USA only.
Opaque shapeID hashes with a shapeName, no code that matches CCKP's, a different licence for each country, and 'Taiwan Province' inside China.
Not usable at all: redistribution is not allowed without prior permission.

countries_with_odd_cases: India: CCKP has 35 units, with no Jammu and Kashmir or Ladakh (IND.11515 is missing); in V1, Jammu and Kashmir is in the disputed-areas layer. India includes Telangana.
Brazil: 4 'Name Unknown' units are islands (BRA014–017, folded into states in 2026 in v2).
China: CCKP has no unit for Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan.

weighting_findings.area_weighted: CCKP's values are area-weighted ('fractional overlap' of grid cells plus 'cosine of latitude' weighting). The heat threshold indicators (hd35, hd40, tr26, hi39, txx, swbgt32) come only as climatology, anomaly, timeseries, trend and year-of-change. There is no population-weighted version of them.
weighting_findings.popwgt_products: CCKP has population-weighted (popwgt) products only for the heatwave variable ehf2: climatologypopwgthw85exposure and climatologypopwgthw3x85exposure. Example code: cmip6-x0.25_climatology_ehf2_climatologypopwgthw85exposure_annual_2040-2059_median_ssp245_ensemble_all_mean. They are absolute person-days, not an average per resident: India 38,915,194,880; Delhi 110,786,096; Kenya 1,255,721,088 (2040–2059, SSP2-4.5).
weighting_findings.right_pairing: They pair with the area-weighted climatologyhw85exposure (India 12.55, Delhi 7.73), not with climatologyhwdays (India 37.35, Delhi 20.92).
weighting_findings.population: CCKP does publish population: the pop-x0.25 collection, as pop-x0.25_climatology_popcount_climatology_annual_{period}_mean_{ssp}_gpw-v4_rev11_mean, for countries and regions, 1995–2014 and each SSP period. Delhi 2040–2059 SSP2-4.5 is 14,199,143; Kenya 76,501,020. Delhi person-days divided by population is 7.80, close to its area value of 7.73. Dividing is still our own computation across two CCKP files.

national_totals_problem.finding: CCKP's national totals for count-type values are 2–3 times the sum of its own regions, for both population and person-days. India's person-days are 38.9 billion nationally against 19.36 billion summed over regions. The verification pass said: 'Do not publish CCKP national population or person-day totals.' It also said area-averaged values are likely unaffected, but did not test that.

weighting_findings.consequence: Use area-averaged values only, label them as such, and reject the count-type variables (popcount, popwgt and anything ending in exposure) in the pipeline.

rendering_tools.note: From the boundary pass (2026-10-15). At that date web/package.json had only d3-scale, d3-shape and motion, and the pipeline had none of these tools; geo.py read only the .dbf attribute file.
web: d3-geo 3.1.1 (ISC), includes geoEqualEarth: 36,329 B minified, 13,100 B gzipped.
Reference: world-atlas@2.0.2 countries-110m.json is 107,761 B (38,423 B gzipped) with 177 countries and numeric ISO ids; countries-50m.json is 756,420 B (232,879 B gzipped).
pipeline: Python topojson 2.2 on shapely 2.2 (BSD-3), using prequantize and toposimplify.

Topology-aware simplification is needed so neighbouring regions share one simplified border; per-polygon shapely.simplify leaves slivers and gaps. Record the tolerance and quantisation as the transformation applied.
rendering_tools.file_counts: The first pass proposed data/v1/geo/world.json and about 250 data/v1/geo/adm1/<ISO3>.json files. That takes the file count from 4,731 in today's out/ to about 4,980, against the 15,000 limit in web/scripts/check-build.mjs, with every file far below 20 MiB. The build plan later set a budget of about 5,370 files.

decisions.decision: Take the projected values from CCKP's CMIP6 ensemble (registered as wb-cckp), through its API, for countries and for states or provinces.
decisions.why: It is the only open source found with future values for every country and 3,527 regions, under CC BY 4.0. IIASA's Climate Solutions Explorer has no states or provinces; the IPCC Atlas has only IPCC reference regions.

decisions.decision: Seven measures, each as a country indicator and a region indicator: future.wb-cckp.{hot-days-35c, hot-nights-26c, heat-index-39c-days, hottest-day, wettest-day, longest-dry-spell, warming}-{countries|regions}.
decisions.why: The ids follow the data plan, with the suffix -regions rather than -adm1. The wettest day was withheld later in the build (see open_questions).

decisions.decision: Dimension scenario: historical, ssp126, ssp245, ssp585. Windows: 1995/2014 (historical only, none for warming), 2020/2039, 2040/2059, 2060/2079, 2080/2099. The median is the value, p10 is lower and p90 is upper, with the interval named 'range'. Status is final for the historical run and projection otherwise.
decisions.why: Windows and paths as the plan set them. The plan gives no reason for leaving out SSP1-1.9 and SSP3-7.0; the first note found that SSP1-1.9 has only the ensemble, with no per-model runs.

decisions.decision: Scenario labels come from the pipeline: 'SSP1-2.6, low emissions', 'SSP2-4.5, middle emissions', 'SSP5-8.5, very high emissions' and, for the past, 'Model simulation of 1995–2014, not observations'. The path icons are shapes only.
decisions.why: The words must be the data's words. Whether 'very high' or 'high' is right for SSP5-8.5 is left to the owner (see open_questions).

decisions.decision: Use area-averaged values only, labelled so. No population-weighted values this round.
decisions.why: CCKP has no population-weighted threshold indicators, its population-based heatwave values are inflated nationally, and the only population-weighted source (IIASA) has no states or provinces.

decisions.decision: The pipeline reads an explicit variable allowlist and always rejects popcount, popwgt and anything ending in exposure. CCKP's national population and person-day totals are never published.
decisions.why: National count-type totals are 2–3 times the sum of CCKP's own regions (see weighting_findings).

decisions.decision: Draw the map on World Bank GAD V1: admin-0 for the world map, admin-1 per country. Do not use v3, Natural Earth, geoBoundaries or GADM for the regions.
decisions.why: V1 is the only file whose codes join to CCKP's. The first boundary note recommended Natural Earth 50m admin-0 for the world layer and v3 admin-1 for regions; the verification pass made that obsolete. Drawing a country's outline from the same set as its regions also avoids the disagreement at India, Western Sahara and other disputed edges.

decisions.decision: Join in this order: (1) the GAUL rule, (2) the ADM1CD rule, (3) declared pairs, (4) an exact name match after normalisation that is unique on both sides. A code match counts only when the names agree. The build stops if the two code rules point at different features, if a feature is used twice, or if a pair is unresolved; each unresolved pair must be declared accept or reject in pipeline/geo/cckp-adm1-declared.csv. The result is written to data/v1/geo/cckp-adm1-crosswalk.csv.
decisions.why: A code match whose names differ (Orissa and Odisha, say) would otherwise fall through to 'unjoined' and the shape would disappear without anyone noticing. A .prj that is not WGS84 also stops the build.
decisions.from: build plan, section 1 item 6 and Phase 2

decisions.decision: The 68 placeholder names become 'Unnamed region of {Country} ({code})' in the entity table and are left out of search. The 32 DIS.* units are left out of the entity table by a declared rule and drawn as a grey, dashed 'Disputed area (World Bank), not coloured'.
decisions.why: The DIS.* units do have values, so a disputed shape must not say 'No data'.
decisions.from: build plan, section 1 item 9 and section 2

decisions.decision: Three map states. Disputed area: grey fill, dashed edge, 'Disputed area (World Bank), not coloured'. No value: hatched, 'No data for X in the World Bank's Climate Change Knowledge Portal'. A World Bank shape with no CCKP region joined: hatched, 'CCKP's regions do not match this shape; its values are listed beside the map'.
decisions.why: Rule 8: the UI says what is missing and never substitutes another value.

decisions.decision: Keep region views inside the country's file (future/c-<ISO3>.json), not as separate region node files. URL: /?mode=future&p=2040-2059&s=ssp245&c=IND&r=IND.11510&m=tr26, with m left out for hd35.
decisions.why: The 3,527 separate region node files would duplicate the country files. The file budget is about 5,370, not about 8,900.
decisions.from: build plan, section 1 item 10 and section 2

decisions.decision: Simplify in the pipeline with a topology-aware tool. Each feature carries a representative point (rp) taken from the unsimplified geometry. Fill shapes without strokes and draw borders as one mesh, with no coastline stroke.
decisions.why: Micro-states (TUV, NRU, MCO, VAT, TKL) collapse when simplified; countries across the 180° line (RUS, FJI, USA, KIR, NZL) show seams in a rotated projection.

decisions.decision: Keep the national-within-regions check as the pipeline gate, and add a diagnostic for fully joined countries that compares CCKP's national value with the area-weighted mean of its regions (geodesic areas). Record the result in docs/sources.md. The docs claim no more than this.
decisions.why: A national mean that is wrongly weighted but stays inside its regions' range passes the first check, so the check is necessary but not sufficient.
decisions.from: build plan, section 1 item 5 and section 4

decisions.decision: Carry the boundary licence's obligations: attribution 'The World Bank: World Bank Official Boundaries (Global Administrative Divisions V1, 2025-05-07): World Bank'; a modification note 'Simplified by Environment Dashboard from …'; a notice with the terms URL; no logo; no endorsement; mirror_raw true. Use the Dataset Terms page as terms_url and record the catalogue's 'licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0' quote in the YAML header.
decisions.why: The catalogue page is probably rendered by script, so a scripted terms check against it would fail; wb-cckp already checks the Dataset Terms page automatically.
decisions.from: build plan, section 1 item 4 and Phase 2

decisions.decision: No world aggregate this round: the big number at the root is the top-ranked country for the chosen slice.
decisions.why: Registering CCKP's land-only world aggregate (global_land) would cost about 270 more files to fetch; left to the owner (see open_questions).

decisions.decision: No 'so what' card on future views. They carry plain cross-chapter cards to people:hw-<ISO3>, people:coast-<ISO3> and heat:c-<ISO3>, each only when it is in that chapter's ids().
decisions.why: Future views are already about people.

decisions.decision: Drop the pairing of Kulp and Strauss's RCPs with SSPs.
decisions.why: It would be our own equivalence claim.

decisions.decision: Accept that region values stop updating when CCKP moves to the new World Bank boundaries: every region code changes, and region indicators fail and keep their last vintage until someone re-joins them.
decisions.why: The failed source keeps its last validated vintage and says so (rule 8). The owner is asked to confirm (see open_questions).
decisions.from: build plan, section 1 item 18 and section 5

open_questions: 1. Owner decision, flagged: the licence of the World Bank boundaries V1 (2025-05-07) is inferred from the dataset-level CC BY 4.0 and from its hosting on CCKP's open bucket, because the catalogue now lists only v3. The zip has no licence file or readme, and the bucket's AWS registry entry is inconsistent (an ODbL label linking to CC BY 4.0). Do you accept the inference? If not, every country gets ranked bars instead of a region map.

2. Population-weighted values as a follow-up. CCKP has no population-weighted values for hd35, hd40, tr26, hi39, txx or swbgt32, and only absolute person-days for the heatwave variable. The IIASA Climate Solutions Explorer (Zenodo 14524342, v1.1) is the only population-weighted source found: countries only (227, no states or provinces), a 2.39 GB country zip that is a manual acquisition, values tied to warming levels and not to years, and a CC BY 4.0 licence read from its README and not re-verified.
